label: D1 after an unrewarded visit to S2 (not late in the episode)
explanation: Fires only at D1, and only when the previous trial was unrewarded (never after a reward, never at GO/D2). Within that, it is specific to the previous trial having reached S2: S2 unrewarded gives precision ~0.75 (0.88 with ep_trial < 85); it almost never fires after S1 unrewarded. The ~18% of activations it misses are on the first trial of each window, where prev_state is not recorded in the window (the agent did observe it). Using prev_state != 1 to include those gives dev F1 0.86 / mass recall 0.996, but I recorded the cleaner prev_state == 2 version (dev F1 0.85, precision 0.88). The rate drops late in the episode (almost silent at trials 85-99), so the ep_trial cutoff is needed. Magnitude is larger when the agent then prefers a1 (policy logit positive, upcoming action a1 holds 83% of mass but only 60% of active steps) and when S1 is the good state. So it looks like an S2-was-unrewarded, so lean toward a1 signal. Uses only observed variables.

issues: The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.880, R 0.816, F1 0.847, mass recall 0.813.

The phase claim holds. Every active step (54104 in dev) is at D1, with zero at GO or D2. It never fires after a reward: prev_reward==1 has 0 active steps. It never fires after S1 unrewarded: (D1 & prev_reward==0 & prev_state==1) scores P 0 and R 0 on test.

Most misses are at rel -3, where prev_state is not recorded inside the window. (D1 & rel==-3 & prev_reward==0) has precision 0.41, which fits roughly half of those being after S2. prev_state != 1 gives test F1 0.858 and mass recall 0.996, which confirms the explanation. Excluding rel -3, recall is close to complete.

The ep_trial cutoff is a gradual fade, not a cliff, and this is where nearly all false positives sit. On rel>-3 steps, base-predicate precision is 0.984 for trials <60, 0.885 for 60-69, 0.587 for 70-79 and 0.345 for 80-84. For trials >=85 it is 0.054. The label's 'not late in the episode' is accurate, but the 85 threshold is arbitrary: <80 gives about the same F1 (0.852 on rel>-3 steps).

Magnitude claims check out: upcoming action a1 has 83% of the activation mass on 60% of active steps, and good==S1 has 77% of the mass. The explanation leaves out one magnitude effect. The case a1 -> rare S2 -> unrewarded holds 61-63% of the mass on about 41% of active steps (test precision 0.949), against 0.829 precision for a2 -> common S2 unrewarded. This fits the 'lean toward a1' reading, because both cases call for choosing a1 next under model-based play.
The predicate uses no future variables. The claim of observed-only variables is correct.
